page.title: Auralis Presence — mmWave room sensing, fall safety, offline autonomy

sections.heading: Four zones, one track
text: Presence tracks position, not just motion, so it holds named zones (Bed, Desk, Kitchen, Entry) through stillness. No camera, no microphone — position, posture, and breathing are the only signals, which is the pitch for [bathrooms and bedrooms](https://github.com/auralis/presence/blob/main/docs/hld.md#overview).
bullets: **Iris MW** acquires a track as the resident steps through the doorway and streams per-frame positions to **Aria MCU**.
Aria MCU maps the position into the room's zone map and marks zone **Entry** occupied.
Aria MCU publishes the `entry → occupied` edge to **Chorus** and mirrors the same event to **Atrium** over the LAN channel.
Chorus delivers the event to **Motif**, which updates the room's zone ledger.
The resident crosses to the desk; Aria MCU emits `entry → clear` and `desk → occupied` edge events to both Chorus and Atrium.
Atrium matches `desk occupied` against its cached routine and switches the desk lamp on over Thread — *no cloud round trip*.
Motif streams the zone timeline through Overture to the resident's open app.
The resident sits still reading; Iris MW's micro-motion sensing keeps Desk occupied where a **PIR** would have timed out to vacant.

sections.heading: A fall, a check-in, a phone tree
text: The machine never calls first — a 60-second human check-in sits between detection and the escalation ladder, and vitals ride the case the whole way.
bullets: **Iris MW**'s posture estimator sees the track's height collapse from 1.7 m to 0.4 m by the shower and flags a fall hypothesis to **Aria MCU**.
Aria MCU runs a *30-second* on-device confirmation window — sudden height drop and no recovery motion.
Confirmation holds; Aria MCU publishes `evt/room/safety` (fall, confidence 0.93, zone Shower) to **Chorus** at QoS 1.
Chorus delivers to **Motif**, which forwards safety events straight to **Vigil**; Vigil opens a case.
Vigil starts the human check-in: **Encore** pushes `Are you OK? — respond within 60 s` to the resident's phone while **Atrium** speaks the same prompt in the room.
No response arrives, and Iris MW still reports a prone target with breathing micro-motion, which Aria attaches to the case as live telemetry.
The check-in window expires; Vigil dials the first emergency contact with zone, time, and vitals summary.
No answer within 90 s; Vigil dials the second contact, who accepts and confirms they are heading over.
Vigil marks the case *engaged* and streams live occupancy to that contact's app until Iris MW reports an upright, moving track again.
Aria reports recovery; Vigil closes the case and writes the full timeline — hypothesis to closure — to the ledger.

sections.heading: The night, measured
text: The same radar that tracks walking drops to 2 Hz and reads breathing — one sensor, two sampling modes, one morning summary.
bullets: At **23:10** the track settles into zone Bed; Aria MCU switches Iris MW into 2 Hz breath-sensing mode.
Aria MCU publishes `sleep/session-start`; Chorus delivers it to **Tempo**, which opens the night's record.
Overnight, Aria batches respiration-rate and restlessness samples to Tempo *every 10 minutes*.
A restless spell at **04:12** is folded into the record as a wake event.
At **07:40** the track leaves Bed; Aria publishes `session-end`, Tempo finalizes the record, and **Encore** delivers the morning summary.
Separately, Tempo's inactivity watcher scores each daytime hour's zone activity against the resident's rolling baseline.
By **12:00** no Kitchen occupancy has been seen on a day the baseline expects it; Tempo raises an inactivity flag to **Vigil**.
Vigil runs the same ladder as a fall, but starts at the gentle end — an app check-in, then contacts — because inactivity is a slow signal.

steps.text: 23:10 — track settles into Bed; Iris drops to breath mode
session-start opens the night's record at Tempo
Respiration + restlessness batch up every 10 min to Tempo
04:12 — restless spell folded in as a wake event
07:40 — Bed clears; session-end finalizes the record
Morning summary lands; the inactivity watcher takes over the day

sections.heading: The internet goes away
text: The hub is the failover brain — automations and the safety ladder keep working on the LAN, and the cloud gets an honest, timestamped backfill afterward.
bullets: The ISP drops at **20:12**; Aria MCU's Chorus session times out and its cloud link flips to `OFFLINE` while the LAN channel to Atrium stays up.
Atrium also loses Chorus and switches to *local-authority mode* — its cached routine set becomes the only automation engine.
The resident walks into the kitchen; Aria sends `kitchen → occupied` to Atrium over the LAN and the lights routine fires in **~40 ms**.
Aria MCU appends every zone event to its *4-hour* flash store-and-forward buffer.

A fall during the outage stays local: **Vigil** is unreachable, so **Atrium** runs the degraded ladder itself — spoken prompt, then siren and strobing lights; *it cannot dial contacts without internet*.
Connectivity returns at **21:03**; Aria reconnects to Chorus and drains the buffer oldest-first, each event carrying its original timestamp.
Motif reconciles the backfill into the ledger with the span marked `backfilled`; Tempo recomputes the sleep/inactivity windows it overlaps.
Vigil reviews the buffered fall case, finds it resolved locally (the resident got up at **20:41**), and files it with a note instead of paging anyone.
**Internet drops** — the honest loss is outbound calling: *no contact is dialed until the link returns*, and the app shows `local mode`.

sections.heading: Failure modes
bullets: **Power fails** — no battery, so the sensor goes dark; **Atrium** raises a lost-sensor alert after *three* missed heartbeats (~90 s), and **Vigil** treats a dark sensor in a care household as a soft check-in trigger, not silence.
**Battery low** — not applicable on the sensor (wall power); **Atrium**'s own backup battery keeps the siren ladder alive *~4 h* into a power cut.
**Chorus or Motif down** — identical to an outage from the sensor's view: buffer and drain; the LAN path is unaffected.
**Vigil down** — **Motif** holds safety events in a dead-letter queue with retry and pages the on-call; **Atrium**'s local ladder is the household backstop.
**Track confusion** — two people merging into one track demotes tracker confidence; automations still fire, but safety classification pauses rather than guess.
